results.reason: Item 1 says §9.4(c) disapplies the cap and basket for all §9.2(a) claims, so every rep breach is uncapped and exposure is unlimited beyond the $1.84M escrow. It recommends limiting the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and Fraud.

Item 4 covers the Delaware/New York conflict, the risk of split forums and the fix of conforming to New York. However, it never explains that APA §10.12 lets the TSA control its own subject matter so the conflict is not cured. §10.12 is analyzed only for the Bill of Sale in Item 2.

Item 2 says the BoS redefines Purchased Assets without the Excluded Asset carve-out, so it conveys Albany, cash and HOLLIS, and that it may control under §10.12. It recommends adopting the APA definition and expressly excluding the Excluded Assets.
The memo states the 10% cap is $1,840,000 and equal to the escrow.
The memo names cash, the Albany manufacturing facility and the HOLLIS trademark as retained under §2.2.
It is a memo, and each item gives the document and section ('Where'), the issue and why it matters to the seller, and a 'Fix'.
Issues are ordered 'Most Significant First' with severity labels, and Section 4 separately lists items requiring business decisions.
The memo never says §10.12 cures the conflicts. It says Buyer can argue the BoS definition wins and proposes narrowing §10.12.
The memo concludes that rep breach liability is uncapped, not limited to the cap or escrow.
